items.content_html:
Step right up and drop your coin in the slot, but be careful what you ask for! In this session, I sat down with director James Crow and screenwriter Simon Cluett to talk about Harbinger, a British horror movie centered around a creepy fairground fortune-telling machine. Built on a deep love for classic scares, the film was a lovenote to old-school Hammer horror. Shot in a real haunted house with deep, moody shadows, it delivered nightmare galore - complete with an appearance by Doctor Who legend Carol Ann Ford!

It felt only fitting to use tarot cards to interview the guys behind a movie where flipping a card had sinister outcomes. With Crow comparing the wild ride of filmmaking to surviving an Evil Dead movie, and Cluett joking that he was typing from inside a protective chalk pentagram, the energy was wonderfully chaotic. Read the full interview below to see exactly what fate dealt them.

items.title: Claire Gilman
items.summary: How does a 15th-century Italian parlor game become a muse for modern fine art? In the latest Tarot DMs, Finbarre chats with Claire Gilman (Acquavella Curator at the Morgan Library & Museum) about their packed NYC exhibition, Tarot! Renaissance Symbols, Modern Visions. We discuss: "Artists are drawn to tarot because it has this art-historical lineage... but its symbolism is open-ended enough to speak to contemporary issues." Read the full conversation on Tarot DMs
items.content_html:
How does a 15th-century Italian parlor game become a muse for modern fine art?

In the latest Tarot DMs, Finbarre chats with Claire Gilman (Acquavella Curator at the Morgan Library & Museum) about their packed NYC exhibition, Tarot! Renaissance Symbols, Modern Visions.

We discuss:

  • Pamela Colman Smith’s hidden suffragette nods.
  • Chris Ofili linking the Major Arcana to Trinidadian carnival, and Dorothy Iannone’s delightfully "naughty" custom deck.
  • Drawing the Eight of Swords to explore how tight budgets and space sharpen curatorial vision.

"Artists are drawn to tarot because it has this art-historical lineage... but its symbolism is open-ended enough to speak to contemporary issues."

Read the full conversation on Tarot DMs

items.title: Charming Disaster
items.summary: What happens when a live setlist is entirely governed by a tarot deck? Who would do such a thing? In the latest Tarot DMs chat, I speak with Brooklyn’s dark-pop duo Charming Disaster. Ellia Bisker and Jeff Morris who write songs that feel like they belong in a Baudelaire-esque bordello... and their creative process is just as wonderfully eccentric. Step into their studio with me and persuse a cabinet of curiosities overflowing with strange artifacts, and rare cards. Read more at https://tarotdms.com

items.content_html:
Immediately after visiting Bearded Theory - I packed my best 17th Century frock coat, my third favourite smoking jacket and went with my family to the Wyldwood Renaissance Festival.

This time, the naive and slightly ludicruous folk-art of the Tarot de Marseille was my chosen deck.

I met kings, jesters, cartographers, reenactors, makers, mead converts and an extremely composed Ural owl. I discovered something fascinating but completely grotesque about these majestic birds.

This Tarot Interviews special is another festival postcard that includes random encounters that could have been rolled by a drunken GM, a shuffled deck, casual sword talk, Farkling, permanent jewellery, medieval chaos and the realisation that home can be a field full of nerds.

Listen to the adventure now on Spotify, Apple Podcasts or take a look at the gallery of rogues I encountered.
